modules.title: Name the whole
modules.desc: Identify the whole, then read a fraction as equal parts OF that whole.
modules.rule: A fraction a/b means the whole is cut into b EQUAL parts and we take a of them.
teach: Always start by naming the whole: 'The whole is all 8 slices' or 'the whole is the chocolate bar'.
The bottom number (denominator) tells how many EQUAL parts the whole is cut into.
The top number (numerator) tells how many of those equal parts we are talking about.
contrast: If the parts are NOT equal, you cannot name a simple fraction yet.
modules.transfer: Draw a bar, cut it into 6 equal parts, shade 5. Which fraction did you make?

modules.title: Part and the rest
modules.desc: Shaded + unshaded = the whole, so the two parts always add back to 1.
modules.rule: If a/b is shaded then (b-a)/b is unshaded, and a/b + (b-a)/b = 1 (the whole).
teach: The shaded part and the leftover part together ALWAYS make the whole whole.
Read the question slowly: does it ask for the shaded part or the part that is left?
Same denominator for both parts - only the top numbers share out the whole.
contrast: Give what is LEFT when a story says 'gives away' - that is the complement.
modules.transfer: A pizza has 10 equal slices and 7 are eaten. Write the eaten part and the part left.

modules.title: Equivalent fractions
modules.desc: Multiply (or divide) the top AND bottom by the SAME number to rename a fraction.
modules.rule: a/b = (a*k)/(b*k): scaling top and bottom by the same k keeps the value the same.
teach: To rename a fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the SAME number.
You can also go smaller by dividing top and bottom by the same number (simplify).
Adding the same number to top and bottom does NOT keep the value - that changes it.
contrast: 3/4 is NOT 4/5 - you may not add 1 to top and bottom.
modules.transfer: Find three fractions equal to 1/2 by scaling. What do you multiply by each time?

modules.title: Compare fractions
modules.desc: Same denominator: compare the tops. Different: rename to a common denominator first.
modules.rule: With equal denominators the larger numerator wins; otherwise make the denominators match.
teach: If the bottoms are the same, the bigger TOP number is the bigger fraction.
If the bottoms differ, rename both to a common denominator, THEN compare the tops.
A bigger bottom number does NOT mean a bigger fraction - it means smaller equal parts.
contrast: 1/8 < 2/5 even though 8 > 5 - bigger denominator means SMALLER slices.
modules.transfer: Compare 2/3 and 3/5 by giving both the denominator 15. Which is greater?

modules.title: Add and subtract LIKE fractions
modules.desc: Same denominator: add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom the same.
modules.rule: a/d +/- b/d = (a +/- b)/d - the denominator (the size of each part) never changes.
teach: When the bottoms match, add (or subtract) only the TOP numbers.
Keep the SAME bottom - the size of each equal part has not changed.
Never add the bottoms together - 1/6 + 4/6 is not 5/12.
modules.transfer: Fill a 10-part bar: 3/10 then 4 more tenths. How many tenths now?

modules.title: Add and subtract UNLIKE fractions
modules.desc: Rename to a common denominator FIRST, then add or subtract the tops.
modules.rule: To combine a/b and c/d, rewrite both over a common denominator, then add/subtract tops.
teach: You cannot add across different bottoms - first give both fractions the same bottom.
Use a denominator both bottoms divide into (a common multiple).
Once the bottoms match, add or subtract only the tops.
contrast: 1/2 + 1/3 is NOT 2/5 - rename to sixths first: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.
modules.transfer: Rewrite 1/3 and 1/4 over 12, then add. What common denominator did you use?

modules.title: Mixed and improper fractions
modules.desc: Mixed to improper: whole*bottom + top. Improper to mixed: divide to find the whole.
modules.rule: w a/b = (w*b + a)/b; and n/b = (n//b) and remainder/b as a mixed number.
teach: To make an improper fraction, multiply the whole by the bottom, THEN add the top.
Keep the same bottom number the whole way through.
Do not just stick the whole in front of the top - 2 3/5 is not 23/5.
modules.transfer: Turn 3 2/7 into an improper fraction, then turn it back. Did you return to the start?

modules.title: Fraction OF a quantity
modules.desc: 'of' means multiply: split the whole into bottom parts, then take top parts.
modules.rule: a/b OF q = split q into b equal groups (q/b), then take a groups (a * q/b).
teach: 'of' tells you to multiply the fraction by the quantity.
Divide the quantity by the BOTTOM to make one equal part, then take TOP of them.
Do not divide by the top only - that skips the bottom (the number of parts).
modules.transfer: Find 2/5 of 30 by first finding 1/5 of 30. What is one-fifth first?

questions.title: A chocolate bar
questions.story: A chocolate bar is split into 4 equal squares. Riya eats 1 square.

stages.prompt: What is the whole in this story?
stages.hint: The whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar - the full group before we pick any part.

options.text: all 4 equal squares of the bar
options.feedback: Yes - the whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar, all of it together.
That is the PART we are naming, not the whole it comes from.
That is a number from the story, but it is not the whole group.

stages.prompt: How many EQUAL parts is the whole cut into?
stages.hint: Count every equal part, shaded and not: there are 4.

options.feedback: Right - all 4 equal parts make the bottom number.
That is only the shaded parts. The bottom counts EVERY equal part.

options.text: The parts are not equal, so we cannot say
options.feedback: In this picture the parts ARE equal, so we can count them.

stages.prompt: Which fraction names the shaded part?
stages.hint: Top = shaded (1); bottom = all equal parts (4).

options.feedback: Yes - 1 shaded out of 4 equal parts is 1/4.
The top and bottom are swapped. Top is the shaded count, bottom is the total.
The bottom should be the TOTAL equal parts, not shaded added to total.

worked: The whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar.
It is cut into 4 equal parts, so the bottom number is 4.
1 of those parts are shaded, so the top number is 1.
questions.check: Shaded 1/4 and the bottom 4 counts every equal part.
questions.explain: Why must the parts be equal before we write a fraction?
